subsystems.name: Mechanosynthetic manipulators
subsystems.role: pick, place and bond individual atoms or molecular fragments.

subsystems.name: Feedstock handling
subsystems.role: delivers specific molecules to the assembly site and removes waste.

subsystems.name: Assembly environment
subsystems.role: keeps the workspace clean and controlled.

subsystems.name: Control and programming
subsystems.role: converts a design into step-by-step manipulation commands.

subsystems.name: Energy and heat management
subsystems.role: supplies energy for bond formation and removes excess heat.

buildSteps.title: Demonstrate mechanosynthetic reactions
buildSteps.detail: Use a scanning tunneling microscope to form and break individual bonds between specific atoms, proving the chemistry works.

buildSteps.title: Design molecular manipulators
buildSteps.detail: Synthesize molecules with a reactive tip and a handle that can be positioned by external fields.

buildSteps.title: Build a single-molecule assembler
buildSteps.detail: Combine manipulator, feedstock delivery and control in a vacuum chamber to assemble a small molecule atom-by-atom.

buildSteps.title: Parallelize the manipulators
buildSteps.detail: Fabricate arrays of thousands of independent manipulators on a chip to speed up assembly.

buildSteps.title: Develop feedstock molecules
buildSteps.detail: Create stable, reactive building blocks that can be broken apart and reassembled without side reactions.

buildSteps.title: Prototype a nanofactory
buildSteps.detail: Integrate manipulator arrays, feedstock channels and control software into a machine that builds simple objects such as diamond lattices.

buildSteps.title: Scale and program
buildSteps.detail: Increase the number of manipulators and develop software to design and simulate complex objects, with error correction.

prerequisites.why: it can already position a tip and manipulate single atoms, but only one at a time and very slowly.
single bond formation has been demonstrated in the lab, but not as a general, reliable process.
molecules that move in controlled ways exist (Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2016), but they cannot yet build arbitrary structures.
no method exists to build macroscopic objects with every atom in a designed place.
quantum chemistry can predict many reactions, but simulating a whole nanofactory is beyond current tools.

pathway.milestone: atom manipulation with scanning probe microscopes; synthetic molecular machines
pathway.unlocks: basic tools to move and bond single atoms.

pathway.milestone: mechanosynthetic assembly of small molecules with tens of atoms
pathway.unlocks: proof that atom-by-atom building can be programmed.

pathway.milestone: parallel manipulator arrays assembling simple structures like diamondoid rods
pathway.unlocks: speed and complexity beyond single probes.
manufacturing with atomic precision for materials, electronics and medicine — if the physics and engineering can be scaled.
